body.statement: For every \(\bar L\ge L\) and every \(\mathbf z\) compatible under ceiling \(L\), \(\mathcal I_L(\mathbf z)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\bar L}(\mathbf z)\) and \[\inf\mathcal I_{\bar L}(\mathbf z)\le D_1=\inf\mathcal I_L(\mathbf z)\le U_1=\sup\mathcal I_L(\mathbf z)\le\sup\mathcal I_{\bar L}(\mathbf z).\] Therefore \(U_1-D_1\le\sup\mathcal I_{\bar L}(\mathbf z)-\inf\mathcal I_{\bar L}(\mathbf z)\). The same nesting holds for the separable-direct-effect sets after subtracting the factual quantity \(F_1^0(T)\).
body.justification: The ceiling determines the feasible hazard class, so nesting under a conservative larger ceiling is the minimum transparent sensitivity guarantee.
body.gap: MartinussenStensrud2023 uses resolved hazards to identify the cross-arm integral, but it does not compare sharp grouped-data endpoints across alternative numerical intensity ceilings.
body.consumer: Analysts can report the primary interval at an externally calibrated ceiling and a conservative interval at \(\bar L\), with guaranteed nesting rather than an informal robustness comparison.
